A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, Learning Linear Attention in Polynomial Time. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support a complete comparison, including material relocated between the main text and appendices.

before.justification: v1 Section 6 reports original experiments on learning synthetic linear-attention networks, associative lookup and deterministic finite-automata execution.

after.justification: v3 retains original linear-attention and associative-lookup experiments in Section 4 and finite-automata experiments in Appendix G.4.

M1.justification: The cubic feature mapping, least-squares optimization, SVD recovery of attention heads and identifiability certificate are unchanged. The conclusion's feature-map extension is an applicability claim, without a revised algorithm or implemented component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic regression, associative-lookup and DFA-execution tasks. Moving DFA evaluation to Appendix G.4 and repeating an existing plot under Additional Experiments introduce no new coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain multi-head linear attention, multi-layer single-head linear attention, full Transformers and the convex algorithm. The associative-lookup comparison also retains the same head counts. Newly cited architectures are not evaluated as baselines.

E3.justification: The reported settings remain unchanged, including regression configurations N=512, d=2 and N=2048, d=4; associative-lookup sampling and mixtures; and DFA evaluation at 99% next-token accuracy. Training settings match between v1 Appendices D.1–D.2 and v3 G.1–G.2.

E4.justification: The head-versus-depth study, certificate-eigenvalue and full-rank versus low-rank analyses, and DFA complexity sweeps are retained. v3 Figure 3 repeats the existing d=4 convergence plot rather than adding an analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report standard errors over three runs for the attention-learning and associative-lookup comparisons. No changed run counts, seed disclosures, confidence intervals or statistical procedures are introduced.

E6.justification: The plotted results in v1 Figures 1–3 match v3 Figures 1, 2 and 4, including convergence curves, certificate-distance results and DFA token requirements. v3 Figure 3 duplicates Figure 1b; it adds no result entries.

T1.justification: The learnability bounds, identifiability definitions and lemmas, noise/error analyses, and UTM constructions and proofs are retained after relocation and renumbering. The conclusion adds no formal development supporting its feature-map extension claim.

C1.justification: The central PAC-learnability, identifiability and bounded-history UTM claims remain. The new conclusion additionally asserts that the theory extends to arbitrary key/query feature maps, modestly broadening claimed applicability.

C2.justification: The new conclusion discusses custom key-query kernels as a route toward softmax approximation and explicitly acknowledges the distance between the studied model and modern LLMs. Existing interpretations of optimization, identifiability and DFA results remain substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: Feature-extraction pseudocode, optimizer and hyperparameter tables, DFA encoding instructions, and the Llama-based experimental architecture are retained. No new implementation resources, hardware information, training times or code/data access disclosures are supplied.

R1.justification: v3 adds references connecting the motivation to gated/delta linear attention, xLSTM, RetNet and Mamba2, and removes the Luo et al. discussion and citation. The dedicated related-work discussion and central novelty positioning remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are substantially rewritten around two motivating questions. The learning algorithm explanation is consolidated, detailed identifiability and UTM sections move into appendices, DFA experiments move to G.4, and a Conclusion and Limitations section is added.

P2.justification: v3 adopts NeurIPS formatting and substantially redistributes displayed material. Figure 1 changes from adjacent to stacked panels, Figure 2 is resized and recaptioned, the DFA figure moves to the appendix, and an existing convergence panel is duplicated as Figure 3. Algorithms also move within the reorganized document.

improvement.justification: v3 makes the central contribution easier to follow through clearer motivating questions, a consolidated algorithm explanation and a concluding applicability discussion, while retaining the proofs and experimental evidence. The gains are limited: empirical and formal support are unchanged, Figure 3 is redundant, and the new feature-map extension remains undeveloped.
